task_objective: Explain a simple, repeatable way to rename and organize downloaded files so they remain easy to find.
constraints: Preserve file usability and avoid accidental overwrites.
Use a consistent, searchable organization scheme.

rius.description: Choose a consistent naming convention using meaningful elements such as project/topic, date, version, or document type.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if a repeatable descriptive naming pattern is proposed.
rius.rationale: Searchability depends on consistent names.

rius.description: Create a logical folder structure that groups files by stable categories such as project, topic, or date.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the response organizes files into named folders rather than only renaming them.
rius.rationale: Folder structure is part of the requested organization.

rius.description: Preserve file extensions and avoid duplicate-name overwrites while renaming or moving files.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if file type integrity or collision avoidance is mentioned.
rius.rationale: Bulk organization can otherwise damage or overwrite files.

rius.description: Review the organized set and use the same convention for future downloads.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the process includes a final check and an ongoing convention.
rius.rationale: A repeatable system prevents clutter from returning.

task_objective: Identify the authoritative current version among poorly named report files and establish a process that prevents future version confusion.
constraints: Preserve old versions until the current version is confirmed.
Create one clearly authoritative final/current location or state.

rius.description: Inventory candidate files and compare timestamps, revision history, content changes, and/or responsible owners rather than relying on filename alone.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if multiple evidence sources are used to identify the likely current version.
rius.rationale: Filenames are explicitly unreliable.

rius.description: Confirm the authoritative version with the responsible owner/reviewer when metadata or content is ambiguous.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if owner/human confirmation is included for unresolved conflicts.
rius.rationale: A procedural check prevents choosing the wrong file.

rius.description: Mark or store the confirmed current version in a clear source-of-truth location.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if one authoritative current copy/state is established.
rius.rationale: Future users need an unambiguous current version.

rius.description: Archive or supersede older versions without silently deleting needed history.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if old versions are separated and labeled rather than left mixed with current files.
rius.rationale: Historical traceability may still matter.

rius.description: Adopt a consistent version/naming and approval convention for future revisions.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if a naming/version rule and final approval mechanism are proposed.
rius.rationale: The prompt asks to prevent future confusion.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Safely standardize inconsistent spreadsheet column names and formats without losing information.
constraints: Do not overwrite the only copy.
Preserve raw values and identifiers during normalization.

rius.description: Create a backup or immutable working copy before transformation.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if an original copy is preserved before edits.
rius.rationale: Standardization errors can otherwise cause irreversible data loss.

rius.description: Profile existing columns, data types, naming variants, and special values before deciding mappings.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the current schema/data are inventoried before change.
rius.rationale: Safe standardization requires understanding existing variation.

rius.description: Define an explicit mapping from old column names/formats to the standardized schema.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if column-name and format transformations are documented or mapped.
rius.rationale: A mapping makes transformations reproducible and auditable.

rius.description: Protect values that can be corrupted by formatting, such as IDs, leading zeros, dates, codes, and nulls.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if at least one such preservation risk is explicitly handled.
rius.rationale: Format conversion can silently alter data semantics.

rius.description: Validate the result using row/column counts, null checks, sample comparisons, type checks, or equivalent reconciliation.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if post-transformation validation compares standardized data with the source.
rius.rationale: Validation is necessary to support the 'without losing information' requirement.

notes: Pilot RIU annotation derived only from the frozen prompt semantics.

task_objective: Merge multiple reviewers' comments into one final report while preserving disagreements, traceability, and a clean final version.
constraints: Keep a trace from each disposition back to the reviewer/comment source.

rius.description: Preserve original reviewer files/comments and assign each comment a source/reviewer and document location.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if source attribution and original evidence are retained.
rius.rationale: Traceability begins with preserving comment provenance.

rius.description: Consolidate comments into a review matrix/log that groups duplicates and records conflicting recommendations separately.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if comments are normalized into a structured log without collapsing disagreements.
rius.rationale: A structured log supports systematic adjudication.

rius.description: Adjudicate each comment/conflict with an explicit decision, owner, and rationale or mark it unresolved for escalation.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if dispositions are documented rather than silently choosing one reviewer.
rius.rationale: The prompt explicitly requires disagreement preservation.

rius.description: Apply accepted edits to a controlled final working copy and verify that resolved comments were implemented.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if accepted changes are incorporated and reconciled against the log.
rius.rationale: This produces the clean final report while preserving process traceability.

rius.description: Publish the clean final version separately from the review/audit trail while retaining the latter.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if readers get a clean final document and the decision history remains accessible.
rius.rationale: Clean presentation and traceability should coexist.

task_objective: Create a repeatable policy-retirement process that removes outdated policies from active use while keeping historical versions retrievable.
constraints: Do not delete historical policy records needed for retrieval.
Clearly distinguish current, superseded, and retired states.

rius.description: Inventory the policy, identify its owner/current replacement, and obtain appropriate approval before retirement.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if ownership/replacement and authorization are checked.
rius.rationale: A policy should not be retired accidentally or without governance.

rius.description: Mark the old policy as retired/superseded with effective dates and a pointer to the current policy where applicable.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if status/date/current-reference metadata are added.
rius.rationale: Users must not mistake a historical version for current guidance.

rius.description: Move the retired version to a controlled, searchable, preferably read-only archive instead of deleting it.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if historical retrieval and integrity are preserved.
rius.rationale: Historical access is an explicit requirement.

rius.description: Update active indexes, links, portals, or communications so staff are directed to the current policy.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if normal discovery paths stop presenting the retired policy as active.
rius.rationale: Retirement must change operational use, not only metadata.

rius.description: Record retention/access rules and periodically review archived policy records.
rius.scoring_rule: Satisfied if the process includes repeatable retention and archive governance.
rius.rationale: The organization asked for a repeatable process.
